changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: Do not lead with an average. Offer to size the prospect's own losses instead: Send us three months of your declined orders and we'll show you what the orders dying at the last step are worth to you, and how much of that we can win back. Use this with ecommerce champions whose finance lead makes the final call.
changes.why: We showed the average-uplift slide, but the CFO still saw 'the same thing', even though Farah had offered to put a figure on the failed orders from a three-month export.

changes.change: Add a one-page business case the champion can hand to finance, built on the prospect's own data before any pricing goes out. It should show the value of failed orders, especially the big baskets, next to our price, so finance never sees our quote as the only thing from us. Use it whenever the decider will not take vendor meetings.
changes.why: The champion asked for 'a one-page business case' and was sent the deck and pricing instead, and the CFO, who never met us, decided on a controller's page where our quote was the only thing from us.

changes.change: Add a line for prospects on a bank-provided processor, used early before the incumbent counters: A better rate from your current processor still leaves the same orders failing at checkout. The question is what the card says no to, not just what each transaction costs.
changes.why: Once the bank sharpened the rate with 'No new product, nothing', the conversation moved from why big orders fail to the rate, and we never pulled it back.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For inbound prospects whose checkout orders are failing at the payment step, open with lost revenue instead of global growth: You do all the work to get someone to buy, and then the card says no. Let's find out what those orders are worth, starting from your own dashboard.
changes.why: The deal started with the champion's own dashboard showing one in twelve online orders failing, worse on the big baskets, and her greenhouse line describes that cost far more sharply than a global-growth opener does.
